findings.title: Persistent-profile RED has no durable room-head floor, so the pending pair after restart is either nonexistent or test-authored
findings.evidence: createDirectRoomHeadControl() returns { fault, operations, state: null } and directRoomHeadAuthority (871-947) mutates only that in-memory object; the same control instance is handed to the reopened room in directPendingRecovery (1185-1210), which is the same-realm approximation the audit says must be replaced. The only other authority, examples/v3-chat/src/index.ts:741, is a closure-scoped let state. No durable V3RoomHeadAuthority exists (no RoomHead owner in packages/storage/src or packages/storage-browser/src). After a genuine process kill the reopened process therefore has no pending floor: with initialization create the state resets to genesis epoch 0 and with migrate it is pending===null at stable epoch 2, so examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:1573-1581 fails with D110C_FLOOR_MISMATCH instead of reaching recoverPendingCreatorSuccessorAdoption. The only mechanically working alternative is re-authoring control.state after the restart from pre-crash values, as d110cFloorMatrix already does at 1158-1168 and directHeadAhead at 1273 - which makes the authenticated pending room-head pair a test artifact created after the crash, so both the RED failure and the GREEN pass would be satisfiable by fixture-authored positive state rather than by durable resume. The plan names no owner for this (it lists only the retained failBeforePublication and commit fault seams) while forbidding any floor/authority change, and 0b0's production floor-owner selection is still explicitly open.
findings.required_action: Amend the plan subsection to name the durable restart floor explicitly before RED: (a) state that the persistent-profile fixture owns a durable, origin-scoped room-head floor written solely by the production beginRoomHeadAdvance path before the crash and re-read verbatim by the new process, with the test forbidden from constructing or mutating any pending/stable value after the restart; (b) require the GREEN to assert that the post-restart floor is byte-identical to the pre-crash begin result and that no other floor value reaches the pending pin; (c) require the reopened process to re-derive the snapshot declaration and all store handles locally rather than receiving any pre-crash serialized value; and (d) state that this fixture floor is test-owned evidence only and does not select or pre-empt D.110c-0b0's production floor owner.

findings.title: v3-room pins no-pending cold reopen to stable epoch exactly 1, so the post-adoption state this slice creates is unreopenable
findings.evidence: When successorSnapshotDeclaration is defined and pending===null, reopen refuses unless openedRoomHeadState.stable.epoch === 1 (D110C_FLOOR_HEAD_AHEAD or D110C_FLOOR_MISMATCH). 0c's own gate is unaffected because both crash orderings leave pending non-null and the epoch-3 reopen happens in the same session after commitRoomHeadAdvance, but the durable state 0c newly produces (stable epoch 3, pending null) cannot be reopened by any later restart. The plan asserts the existing v3-room composition is already sufficient and lists no owner for this pin, while the umbrella minimum-functional GREEN requires post-adoption restart.
findings.required_action: Record the pin as a named residual limitation of this slice, state that 0c's cold reopen occurs only in-session after the floor commit, and assign generalization of the no-pending reopen epoch check to the named post-adoption restart slice (D.110c-c or D.110c-d) as blocking before any post-adoption restart acceptance.

findings.title: RED terminal classification is a disjunction, so a fixture defect can satisfy the intended failure
findings.evidence: The plan accepts either the pending-invalid or the recovery-unavailable classification. Current production is deterministic: at epoch 2 every candidate fails the genesis opener, recoverPendingCreatorSuccessorMaterial returns kind pending-missing (creator-adoption.ts:1467-1469), and index.ts:2201-2206 maps that to D110C_FLOOR_RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE for both orderings. Accepting D110C_FLOOR_PENDING_INVALID as well lets a mis-authored floor (wrong anchor or epoch, giving chain-invalid or stale-head) satisfy the RED for a reason unrelated to the demonstrated defect.
findings.required_action: Pin the exact expected classification per ordering (D110C_FLOOR_RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE from kind pending-missing) and require the RED to also assert the underlying recovery kind, so any other classification is a fixture failure rather than an intended RED failure.

findings.title: Pending authenticator lacks the reopen owner's current-projection epoch/object/blueprint binding, leaving the substituted-projection case without a deterministic failure
findings.evidence: The reopen owner validates currentProjection.record.epoch, objectId and blueprintDigest against the authenticated anchors (lines 1069-1078). The pending authenticator reads currentProjection only into chain.currentCatalog, which is cross-checked solely by verifiedCatalog (527-548) against the trusted catalog resolution. A substituted current projection carrying the same catalog fields but a different epoch or objectId is therefore accepted, and at N>=1 both the current and successor projections share the kind v3-live-generation-2, so kind uniqueness no longer distinguishes them across closures. The GREEN gate nevertheless requires a substituted-projection adversarial case.
findings.required_action: Add to GREEN step 5 the explicit requirement that the N>=1 path apply the same currentProjection epoch/objectId/blueprintDigest binding as creator-adoption.ts:1069-1078, so the substituted-projection case has a deterministic pre-commit rejection.

findings.title: Audit predicates are file-global substring checks and cannot certify the GREEN change is scoped to the pending authenticator
findings.evidence: Checks such as adoption.includes('currentEpoch: 0,'), adoption.includes('const openedCurrent = openCurrentAnchorTrust({') and adoption.includes('!inspectCreatorTrustAdvance({') match anywhere in a 1500-line file that contains a second, epoch-general reopen owner using the same identifiers. They are true today (I verified the cited lines manually) but cannot distinguish the epoch-0 pins inside authenticatePendingCandidate from identical text elsewhere, so the same pattern reused for GREEN evidence could falsely certify both that the pins were removed and that the epoch-0 branch was preserved.
findings.required_action: Require the GREEN evidence script to scope its predicates to the authenticatePendingCandidate function body (slice between its declaration and the next top-level declaration) and to assert both the removal of the N>=1 pins and the byte-preservation of the epoch-0 branch within that slice.

findings.title: Retained 0b1 obligation to record post-commit signature and pushed-ref identity is deferred rather than satisfied at this checkpoint
findings.evidence: The retained obligation states that the next D.110c evidence checkpoint must retain literal inline audit scripts and record post-commit signature plus pushed-ref identity in its evidence root. This root retains the literal script and command, but records only base and remote_base at the parent ff1a9807; it contains no signature or pushed-ref identity for the plan commit f1e021f2. The plan reassigns that obligation to the GREEN evidence root.
findings.required_action: Add the post-commit signature verification and pushed-ref identity for the plan commit to this evidence root (or to the RED evidence root) and state explicitly that the obligation is satisfied there, so the retained item is not carried forward a second time.
